reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification of every numbered line.

0001 OK - a counterexample is a legitimate way to refute a universal invariance claim ('does not necessarily stay the same').
0002 OK - L(x,y) = (x, x+y) is a well-defined map R^2 -> R^2 (in fact an invertible linear map, matrix [[1,0],[1,1]], det = 1).
0003 OK - blank/formatting line, nothing asserted.
0004 OK - setting up A = (x_A, y_A), B = (x_B, y_B) to check the affine property via differences is the standard criterion.
0005 OK - blank/formatting line, nothing asserted.
0006 OK - computation is correct: L(A) - L(B) = (x_A - x_B, (x_A + y_A) - (x_B + y_B)) = (x_A - x_B, (x_A - x_B) + (y_A - y_B)), i.e. the vector (x_AB, x_AB + y_AB).
0007 OK - the displayed expression is the fixed linear map M(u,v) = (u, u+v) applied to vector AB; L(P) = L(O) + M(OP) for all P, so L is affine. Justified.
0008 OK - blank/formatting line, nothing asserted.
0009 FAILS - the image of the x-axis is computed incorrectly (sign error). Points of Ox are (t, 0), and L(t,0) = (t, t); equivalently, since the inverse is (X,Y) -> (X, Y - X), substituting into y = 0 gives Y - X = 0. So L(Ox) is the line x - y = 0 (i.e. y = x), NOT x + y = 0 as stated. The claim about the y-axis IS correct: L(0,t) = (0,t), so L(Oy): x = 0. Only the first half of this step is wrong.
0010 OK - blank/formatting line, nothing asserted.
0011 OK relative to 0009, but rests on the faulty line: angle(Ox,Oy) = pi/2 is correct, and the angle between the (mis-stated) line x + y = 0 and x = 0 is indeed pi/4. Notably the correct image line x - y = 0 also makes an angle of pi/4 with x = 0, so the numerical value pi/4 happens to be right despite the error in 0009.
0012 OK as a conclusion from 0011 - pi/2 != pi/4 for the two configurations, so the angle is not preserved by this affine map, which is what was to be shown.

Overall: exactly one step (0009) contains a false assertion - the image of the x-axis under L is y = x, not x + y = 0. Under the stated method (INVALID if any step fails), the verdict is INVALID, with the caveat that the defect is a localized sign error and the proof's final conclusion and its numerical value pi/4 remain true after the correction.
